quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #9
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them without training can turn minor injuries into serious ones. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press down on the wound to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: After you pass another car, when is it safe to move back to the right lane?

options.text: After about three seconds.
When you can no longer see the car over your right shoulder.
When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the entire front of the car in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: After passing, return to your lane only when you can see both headlights of the other car in your rearview mirror. Always check your blind spots before moving back.

questions.question: To enter a freeway, you should:

options.text: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
Signal and enter. Freeway traffic must yield to you.
Drive slowly so you can check traffic.
Always stop completely first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, yield to traffic, and enter at the same speed as other cars.
questions.explanation: When entering a freeway, signal and match the speed of other traffic. Always yield to cars already on the freeway.

questions.question: When driving near large trucks, you must allow for:

options.text: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
The shorter distance trucks need to stop.
The quieter sound trucks make.
The higher speed trucks can reach.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer distance trucks need to stop.
questions.explanation: Large trucks need more space to stop. Stay where the truck driver can see you and where large vehicles do not block your view of traffic.

questions.question: When driving where children are playing, expect them to:

options.text: Know when it is safe to cross the street.
Stop at the curb before crossing.
Run into the street in front of you without looking.
Not cross the street unless an adult is with them.

questions.correctAnswerText: Run into the street in front of you without looking.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be extra careful when children are nearby. They may not understand danger and may run in front of your car without looking.

questions.question: You are on a freeway and traffic is merging into your lane. You should:

options.text: Make room for them if you can.
Speed up to keep your place in your lane.
Always stay in your position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make room for them if you can.
questions.explanation: When safe, make room for cars that are merging into your lane.

questions.question: If a car is coming toward you with bright headlights, you should:

options.text: Use your bright lights until they dim theirs.
Flash your lights to warn the other driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass them quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If an oncoming car has bright headlights on, look away from the lights and toward the right side of the road. This keeps you from being blinded.

questions.question: "No zones" are areas around trucks where your car:

options.text: Is hidden in blind spots or is so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
Has enough space to travel safely behind the truck.
Has several car lengths between it and the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is hidden in blind spots or is so close that the truck driver cannot stop or turn safely.
questions.explanation: "No zones" are spots around trucks where your car disappears into the truck's blind spots or is so close it limits the driver's ability to stop and turn safely. Being in a "no zone" greatly increases the risk of a crash.

questions.question: When changing lanes, you should:

options.text: Only use your rearview mirror.
Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
Only use your left side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over your shoulder in the direction you want to move.
questions.explanation: Look over your shoulder to check for cars in your blind spot. You may need to look several times. Watch traffic in front of you and next to you at the same time.

questions.question: A blood alcohol level of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Will not affect your driving.
Will not put other drivers at risk.
Will double your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Will double your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol level nearly doubles your risk of being in a fatal crash.

questions.question: What lane space are motorcycles allowed to use?

options.text: The bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other motor vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have the right to use the same full lane width as all other vehicles.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Merging traffic.
Multiple turns.
Lane shifting.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Merging traffic.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs with black markings tell drivers about road conditions ahead. This sign warns that traffic is merging from the right. Be ready to let traffic merge safely.

questions.question: What do double solid yellow lines mean?

options.text: Passing is permitted from the left.
Passing is permitted from the right.
Passing is not permitted from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is not permitted from either direction.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions. Double solid yellow lines mean no passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.question: As alcohol builds up in your blood, what happens?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down more quickly.
You make fewer driving errors.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your system, your reactions slow down. You may feel more confident, but you will actually make more mistakes while driving.

questions.question: What type of line allows you to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Broken white
Double solid yellow
Solid yellow
Solid white

questions.correctAnswerText: Broken white
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic traveling in the same direction. You can cross broken white lines to pass if the passing lane is clear.

questions.question: What does an orange sign mean?

options.text: There is roadwork ahead.
You must change lanes ahead.
There is a detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is roadwork ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark construction areas. Drive carefully in these areas.

questions.question: What headlights should you use when driving in rain?

options.text: Low beam headlights.
High beam headlights.
Parking lights.
No lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beam headlights.
questions.explanation: Use your low beam headlights when driving in rain.

questions.question: What colors are used on warning signs?

options.text: Black letters or symbols on a white background
Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
White letters or symbols on a blue background
White letters or symbols on a green background

questions.correctAnswerText: Black letters or symbols on a yellow background
questions.explanation: Warning signs have black letters or symbols on a yellow background. Work zone signs have black letters or symbols on an orange background.

questions.question: What should you do when entering a roadway from a private road?

options.text: Blow your horn to warn other cars.
Stop with part of your car on the roadway to alert drivers.
Drive out fast to merge with traffic.
Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians and roadway traffic.
questions.explanation: When entering a roadway from a driveway or private road, you must let pedestrians and roadway traffic go first.

questions.question: How far ahead should you look while driving?

options.text: 10 to 15 seconds ahead.
100 to 150 yards ahead.
One to two blocks ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: 10 to 15 seconds ahead.
questions.explanation: Look 10 to 15 seconds ahead while driving. This helps you see road conditions early and avoid sudden maneuvers.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass.

questions.question: What should you do when you approach a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: You are traveling in the wrong direction.
Treat it like a stop sign.
Wait until it turns green to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign. Come to a complete stop at the stop line or before the crosswalk. Yield to all other traffic and pedestrians.

questions.question: You are angry from something that happened at work. What should you do before driving home?

options.text: Play the radio loudly to distract yourself.
Drive fast on the highway to release stress.
Take a few minutes to calm down.
Have a few drinks at a bar before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to calm down.
questions.explanation: If you are upset or angry, wait until you feel calm before you drive. Driving while angry is dangerous for you and others.

questions.question: Why do you need extra space in front of a large truck?

options.text: To let other drivers merge onto the freeway.
Because the truck needs more distance to stop.
To help other drivers when they want to slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Because the truck needs more distance to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks take longer to stop than cars. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: You want to turn left at an intersection, but oncoming cars block your view. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up when the first lane is clear.
Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
Wait for another driver to wave you across.
Move forward into each lane as it clears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until you can see all lanes are clear before turning.
questions.explanation: Never turn left until you can see that all lanes you need to cross are clear and it is safe to turn.

questions.question: What should you do when driving on slippery roads?

options.text: Use alternate routes.
Drive the same way you do on dry roads.
Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.
Avoid bridges and intersections.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep more distance between you and the car ahead.
questions.explanation: On slippery roads, increase the space between your car and the car ahead. Your car takes longer to stop on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: How should you look ahead to prepare for dangers on the road?

options.text: Scan the whole road and the sides of the road.
Look straight ahead only.
Rest your left foot lightly on the brake pedal.
Focus on the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Scan the whole road and the sides of the road.
questions.explanation: Look far ahead and scan the entire road, including the sides. This helps you spot problems before they become dangerous.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady yellow traffic light?

options.text: Speed up to avoid a red light.
Keep going because you have the right-of-way.
Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
Look at what other cars are doing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stop, unless you are already in the intersection.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means red is coming next. Stop unless you are already in the intersection.

questions.question: What does a single dashed white line between lanes mean?

options.text: You may pass even if it is dangerous.
Lanes go in opposite directions.
You cannot pass.
You may pass if it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may pass if it is safe.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate lanes going the same direction. You may cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What causes many crashes?

options.text: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
Drivers checking mirrors and blind spots.
Drivers yielding the right-of-way.
Drivers keeping a four-second following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers going too fast for the conditions.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because drivers go too fast for road conditions. Always drive within speed limits and slow down when conditions are poor.

questions.question: You can reduce the risk of hydroplaning by:

options.text: Driving through shallow water.
Driving faster.
Driving slower.
Driving through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.

questions.question: You should slow down:

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You should slow down in all these situations: narrow or winding roads, intersections, railroad crossings, hills, sharp curves, areas with pedestrians, and wet or slippery roads.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Winding road ahead.
No parking.
Right lane closed.
Multiple turns ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Winding road ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about upcoming hazards. This sign warns you that the road ahead has curves and you should slow down.

questions.question: Mixing drugs and alcohol while driving:

options.text: Increases crash risk.
Is no more dangerous than alcohol alone.
Makes alcohol less dangerous.
Does not affect your driving ability.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increases crash risk.
questions.explanation: Drugs (illegal, prescription, or over-the-counter) can impair your brain and driving ability. Mixing drugs with alcohol makes the problem worse and increases crash risk.

questions.question: In a roundabout, who does not have to stop?

options.text: A driver going straight across.
A driver entering the roundabout.
A driver already in the roundabout.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver already in the roundabout.
questions.explanation: When entering a roundabout, you must yield to traffic already in it.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: The road gets wider ahead.
The right lane is ending soon.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.
The left lane is ending soon.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon.
questions.explanation: This sign tells you that the right lane will end.

questions.question: A leaking exhaust system can cause:

options.text: Hearing loss.
Pollution.
Carbon monoxide poisoning.
Poor engine performance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Carbon monoxide poisoning.
questions.explanation: The exhaust system removes harmful gases from your vehicle. A leak allows carbon monoxide to enter the passenger area, which is dangerous. Fix any exhaust leaks right away.

questions.question: Your car's rear end is skidding to the left. What should you do?

options.text: Steer to the right.
Steer to the left.
Tap the brakes lightly and shift into neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steer to the left.
questions.explanation: If your car skids, release the brake and steer in the direction you want to go. If the rear skids left, steer left. This straightens the car's direction.

questions.question: A large truck ahead is turning right onto a street with two lanes in each direction. The truck:

options.text: Can finish the turn in either of the two lanes.
May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
Must stay in the right lane while turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: May need to swing wide to complete the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, the rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels. Long trucks need extra space to turn right. They may swing into other lanes to complete the turn.

questions.question: You cannot park:

options.text: On a hill.
In a parking lot.
On a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane.
More than 12 inches from the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to park on a crosswalk or in a marked bike lane. When parking on the street, you must be within 12 inches of the road edge.

questions.question: If a tire blows out, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake hard and hold it.
Hold the steering wheel tight and use light braking.
Pull over quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the steering wheel tight and use light braking.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out while driving, grip the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Slow down gradually by easing off the gas and applying the brakes gently. Do not stop on the road. Pull off to a safe place instead.

questions.question: What happens to your field of vision when you drive faster?

options.text: It gets wider.
It gets narrower.
It makes cross traffic easier to see.
It stays the same.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gets narrower.
questions.explanation: The faster you drive, the narrower your field of vision becomes. As speed increases and vision narrows, you must stay extra alert to dangers around you.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When driving through an intersection.
When passing a bicycle rider.
When a child is about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who do not see you. For example, sound your horn if a child starts to run into the street in front of your car.

questions.question: When can you legally block an intersection?

options.text: If you entered on a green light.
During heavy traffic hours.
Never.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never.
questions.explanation: Do not enter an intersection unless you can drive all the way across before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection is illegal and can result in a ticket.

questions.question: What makes a good defensive driver?

options.text: Driving slowly all the time.
Watching what other drivers are doing.
Driving at the same speed always.
Only driving on roads you know.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watching what other drivers are doing.
questions.explanation: All drivers can get distracted. A defensive driver watches for what other drivers do and prepares for possible problems ahead.

questions.question: What happens when a vehicle hydroplanes?

options.text: Windshield wipers cannot clear the rain.
Tires lose contact with the road.
Spray from trucks blocks your view.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires lose contact with the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a car drives too fast on wet roads and the tires lose all contact with the pavement. The vehicle slides on the water surface.

questions.question: What must you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Keep your speed and stay in your lane.
Move to the right lane and drive slowly.
Pull to the edge of the road and stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the edge of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, pull to the right edge of the road and stop. Stay parallel to the curb. On one-way streets, drive to whichever edge is nearest.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns of hazards ahead.
It marks school zones.
It marks recreation areas.
It shows food and gas locations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns of hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn drivers of hazards they may encounter. These signs are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: What is the maximum speed limit in a school zone when children or crossing guards are present?

options.text: 10 mph
15 mph
20 mph
25 mph

questions.correctAnswerText: 15 mph
questions.explanation: Unless a different speed is posted, the maximum speed limit in a school zone with children and/or crossing guards is 15 miles per hour.

questions.question: What should you do when passing other vehicles?

options.text: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
Honk your horn three times.
Return to your lane within 10 feet of the other vehicle.
You do not need to signal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before passing, check your mirrors and blind spots. Use your turn signal before changing lanes. Return to your lane when you can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.
